title: The Cost of Price Discovery in an LLM Double Auction
abstract: A fixed-value double auction makes unrealised gains from trade measurable, while a token-metered agent economy makes deliberation costly. We combine the accounting of \cite{struski2026competitive} and \cite{hansen2026energy} to identify a testable tension: charging for quote decisions could encourage a profitable spread crossing, but could also remove traders or consume more value than it creates. In the auction's symmetric schedule, the gross surplus ceiling is \(7.5\) per round; its sixth equilibrium trade contributes zero gross surplus. A cost-aware comparison must therefore report realised surplus and inference cost separately, with a stated conversion between their units. We specify the intervention and controls needed to test the behavioural question. No combined experiment has been run, and the direction of its effects remains unknown. % ledger 2, 3, 6, 8, 10, 11, 17, 20
